backlog.spec: In featurize, also compute the full RDKit 2D descriptor vector (Descriptors.CalcMolDescriptors or the descriptor list in rdkit.Chem.Descriptors._descList) for each molecule, replace NaN/inf with 0, clip extreme values to the 0.5/99.5 percentiles of the training set, and concatenate with the Morgan bit vector before fitting the same RandomForestRegressor. Compute the clip bounds inside fit_predict from train_smiles only.
backlog.title: RDKit 2D descriptor set added to Morgan bits

backlog.spec: Replace the fingerprint with about 10 interpretable descriptors known to drive passive permeability: TPSA, MolWt, MolLogP, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, NumAromaticRings, fraction sp3 carbons, formal charge count, and count of carboxylic acid or basic amine groups (via SMARTS). Fit the same random forest on this small matrix; the low-dimensional features may generalize better across unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Small curated physchem descriptor block only

backlog.spec: Switch from GetFingerprintAsNumPy bit vectors to count vectors using gen.GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy with the same radius 2 and 2048 size. Keep the random forest unchanged. Counts keep information about repeated substructures that bit folding discards.
backlog.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprint instead of bits

backlog.spec: Use rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator with an atom invariant generator set to the feature invariants (AllChem.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen or rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen) so pharmacophoric classes (donor, acceptor, aromatic, halogen) replace exact atom identities. Keep radius 2, 2048 bits, and the random forest unchanged.
backlog.title: Feature-Morgan (FCFP) fingerprint

backlog.spec: Increase Morgan radius from 2 to 3 and fingerprint size from 2048 to 4096 bits, keeping the random forest unchanged. Sweep is limited to this single change so the effect of larger substructure context is isolated.
backlog.title: Longer radius and larger hashed fingerprint

backlog.spec: Concatenate several fingerprint types for each molecule: Morgan radius 2 counts (1024 bits), RDKit topological atom-pair counts (1024 bits, rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator), and MACCS keys (167 bits from rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys). Fit the same random forest on the combined matrix.
backlog.title: Multi-fingerprint concatenation

backlog.spec: Replace the Morgan fingerprint with the 167-bit MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys converted to a numpy array). MACCS encodes general functional groups and tends to be less sparse for a small dataset of 728 molecules; keep the random forest unchanged.
backlog.title: MACCS keys alone as features

backlog.spec: Keep the RDKit descriptor plus Morgan feature set, and change max_features from 0.3 to sqrt of the number of features (roughly 0.05 of 2100 columns). Lower fraction gives more decorrelated trees when a few descriptors dominate and many bits are noise.
backlog.title: Random forest with descriptors-plus-fingerprint and feature subsampling tuned

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with ExtraTreesRegressor using the same n_estimators, max_features, and min_samples_leaf, random_state=seed, n_jobs=-1. Extremely randomized split thresholds smooth predictions and often help on small noisy regression sets.
backlog.title: ExtraTrees regressor in place of random forest

backlog.spec: Replace the random forest with LightGBM regressor (objective='regression_l1' so training matches the mean absolute error metric), num_leaves around 15, learning_rate 0.03, n_estimators 600, feature_fraction 0.3, bagging_fraction 0.8 with bagging_freq 1, min_child_samples 10, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8. Use the RDKit descriptor plus Morgan feature matrix.
backlog.title: Gradient boosting with LightGBM on fingerprints plus descriptors

backlog.spec: Use xgboost.XGBRegressor with objective='reg:absoluteerror', max_depth 4, learning_rate 0.03, n_estimators 500, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.3, min_child_weight 3, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8, on the Morgan plus descriptor matrix. Absolute-error objective targets the median, matching the evaluation loss.
backlog.title: XGBoost with absolute-error objective

backlog.spec: Train catboost.CatBoostRegressor with loss_function='MAE', depth 6, learning_rate 0.05, iterations 800, random_seed=seed, verbose=0, thread_count=8, on the RDKit descriptor matrix (about 200 columns) without fingerprints. CatBoost's ordered boosting handles small datasets well and the descriptors carry most of the permeability signal.
backlog.title: CatBoost with MAE loss on descriptors

backlog.spec: Compute the Morgan bit fingerprint as a float matrix, build a Tanimoto (MinMax-style) similarity kernel K(a,b)=sum(min)/sum(max) between training and test sets using numpy broadcasting in chunks, and fit sklearn.svm.SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5, epsilon=0.05) on the training kernel. Chemically meaningful similarity kernels often beat random forests on small molecular datasets.
backlog.title: Support vector regression with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Use the same Tanimoto similarity kernel on Morgan bit fingerprints as in a precomputed-kernel model, and fit sklearn.kernel_ridge.KernelRidge(kernel='precomputed', alpha=0.5) on the training targets after subtracting their mean; add the mean back to test predictions. This is a smooth, closed-form similarity-based regressor with a single regularization knob.
backlog.title: Kernel ridge regression with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Standardize the RDKit descriptor matrix using training-set mean and std (zero-variance columns dropped), then fit sklearn.gaussian_process.GaussianProcessRegressor with kernel ConstantKernel times Matern(nu=1.5) with WhiteKernel, normalize_y=True, n_restarts_optimizer=2, random_state=seed. GP gives smooth interpolation in continuous physchem space.
backlog.title: Gaussian process regression on descriptors with Matern kernel

backlog.spec: Compute Tanimoto similarity between test and training Morgan bit fingerprints, select the k=7 most similar training molecules for each test molecule, and predict a similarity-weighted average (weights = similarity squared) of their measured values. This nonparametric baseline captures local structure-activity trends and is cheap to run.
backlog.title: k-nearest-neighbour similarity regressor

backlog.spec: Standardize the RDKit descriptor matrix on training statistics, clip to plus/minus 5 standard deviations, and train sklearn.neural_network.MLPRegressor with hidden_layer_sizes=(128, 64), activation='relu', alpha=1e-2 (L2), solver='adam', learning_rate_init=1e-3, early_stopping=True with validation_fraction=0.15, max_iter=500, random_state=seed. Average predictions over 3 seeds inside fit_predict.
backlog.title: Multilayer perceptron on descriptors

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, produce out-of-fold predictions on the training data via an internal 5-fold KFold (shuffle, random_state=seed) for three base models: random forest on Morgan bits, LightGBM with MAE objective on the descriptor matrix, and Tanimoto SVR. Fit a non-negative linear regression (scipy.optimize.nnls or sklearn LinearRegression with positive=True) on those out-of-fold predictions and apply the learned weights to base models refit on all training data.
backlog.title: Stacked ensemble of RF, boosting and kernel model

backlog.spec: Train the existing random forest on Morgan bits and a LightGBM regressor with objective='regression_l1' on RDKit descriptors, then return the arithmetic mean of their test predictions. Averaging two dissimilar learners reduces variance without any tuning step.
backlog.title: Simple averaged blend of random forest and gradient boosting

backlog.spec: After fitting the random forest, instead of the mean prediction over trees, return the median of the per-tree predictions for each test molecule (np.median over estimators_ outputs). The metric is mean absolute error, so median aggregation targets the conditional median and is more robust to outlier permeability values.
backlog.title: Median-targeting leaf prediction in random forest via quantile

backlog.spec: Use LightGBM with objective='huber' and alpha set to 1.0 (the Huber delta in log-permeability units) on the Morgan plus descriptor matrix, keeping other settings as a standard small-data configuration (num_leaves 15, learning_rate 0.03, 600 rounds, feature_fraction 0.3). Huber loss down-weights large residuals from outlier molecules while staying close to squared loss near the centre.
backlog.title: Huber loss for gradient boosting

backlog.spec: Train LightGBM (objective='regression_l1') with an internal 10% validation split taken from the training data via KFold-style random split seeded by seed. Use a learning-rate callback that decays the rate geometrically from 0.05 to 0.01 across rounds and stop when the validation MAE has not improved for 50 rounds, then refit on all training data with the best iteration count. Limits overfitting to noise.
backlog.title: Learning-rate decay and early stopping inside boosting

backlog.spec: For LightGBM regression_l1 on descriptors, use a very low learning rate of 0.01 with 2000 rounds and a stronger min_child_samples of 20 and lambda_l2 of 5. Lower step size with more rounds gives smoother fits with the same capacity, which often reduces test MAE on small data at the cost of runtime.
backlog.title: Monotone-free shrinkage via low learning rate with many rounds

backlog.spec: Keep the Morgan plus descriptor features and set RandomForestRegressor min_samples_leaf=3 and max_depth=20 (instead of unlimited depth and leaf size 1). Restricting the tree growth reduces memorization of near-duplicate scaffolds in the training folds and should lower generalization error on held-out skeletons.
backlog.title: Random forest with deeper regularization via leaf size and depth limit

backlog.spec: Before fitting, winsorise train_y at its 2nd and 98th percentiles inside fit_predict, fit the model (for example the random forest on Morgan plus descriptor features) on the clipped targets, and return predictions unchanged. Extreme permeability values in small training sets can distort tree leaf means, so clipping the training target targets the bulk of the distribution better.
backlog.title: Target transformation with winsorised outliers

backlog.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold (rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles) of each training molecule, weight each training sample by 1/sqrt(count of its scaffold) and pass these as sample_weight to the random forest or LightGBM fit. Down-weights over-represented scaffolds so the model does not overfit one ring family.
backlog.title: Sample weighting by scaffold frequency

backlog.spec: For each training molecule generate 4 alternative SMILES strings with Chem.MolToSmiles(mol, doRandom=True, canonical=False) using a seeded random state (set rdkit random seed from seed), compute features for augmented copies with the same target, train the random forest on the augmented set, and predict on canonical test SMILES averaging over test-time augmented variants. Fingerprints are mostly invariant, so this mainly helps descriptor-based models that see atom ordering effects; treat as a check on robustness.
backlog.title: Data augmentation via randomized SMILES

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, train the random forest (keeping Morgan plus descriptor features) with three different random_state values derived from seed (seed, seed+1, seed+2), each with n_estimators=300, and average their test predictions. This reduces the variance of the forest prediction on each fold at roughly triple the runtime, still well within the 10-minute limit.
backlog.title: Average over multiple seeds within fit_predict

backlog.spec: Replace the MLP with a small PyTorch-free NumPy implementation is not allowed, so instead use sklearn MLPRegressor with batch_size=32, solver='adam', learning_rate_init=5e-4 with learning_rate='adaptive', alpha=0.1 (strong L2), hidden_layer_sizes=(64,), and early_stopping=True. Mini-batch gradient steps on standardized descriptors give smoother generalization than full-batch updates on a 728-sample set.
backlog.title: Mini-batch training for neural model with Adam and dropout

incumbent.description: Append the full RDKit 2D descriptor vector to the Morgan bits, with NaN/inf set to 0 and each column clipped to the 0.5/99.5 percentiles of the training fold, before fitting the same random forest.
